properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 25 at 9:42PM MDT until October 25 at 10:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 942 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located near Bitter Lake
Wildlife Refuge, or 9 miles north of Roswell, moving northeast at 15
mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Roswell and Bitter Lake Wildlife Refuge.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 380 between Mile Markers 156 and 176. Highway 285 between
Mile Markers 116 and 125.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 25 at 8:36PM PDT until October 29 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.9ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bay Shoreline locations of San Pablo Bay, San Francisco
Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 11:39 AM
Monday 10/26, 1.8 ft above normal (7.6 ft MLLW) at 12:15 PM
Tuesday 10/27, 1.9 ft above normal (7.7 ft MLLW) at 12:56 PM
Wednesday 10/28, and 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 01:43
PM Thursday 10/29. These predictions include up to 1.0 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:
At 904 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Carlsbad Caverns National Park and Whites City.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 25 at 8:55PM MDT until October 26 at 1:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
Central Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 100 AM MDT.

* At 855 PM MDT, trained weather spotters reported thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches
of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches
are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Roswell.

This includes Highway 380 between Mile Markers 156 and 162.

The heaviest rain has fallen along the Rio Hondo and is expected to
continue downstream into the Roswell area later tonight.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Both localized and distant heavy rainfall will create sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos and over low water crossings.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Georgia Beaches, Beaufort, and Coastal Jasper.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 5 PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Beach erosion is most likely to occur
near the time of high tides.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
West Central Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 145 AM MDT.

* At 750 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Hagerman.

This includes Highway 285 between Mile Markers 87 and 91.

The heaviest rains have occurred along the Lincoln and Chaves County
line due west of Dexter, NM. This heavy runoff is expected to flood
arroyos that flow into the Rio Felix, and expected to reach Hagerman,
NM later tonight into Monday morning.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Both localized and distant heavy rainfall will create sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos and over low water crossings.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Coastal areas of Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara,
and San Luis Obispo Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be Monday
through Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated
Coastal Flood Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger
surf develops.
properties.instruction:

NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Hawaii in Hawaii, HI; Oahu in Honolulu, HI; Kauai, HI; Maui, HI
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 25 at 3:08PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
ESFHFO

A significant pattern change is expected late Monday night through at
least Thursday as deep tropical moisture is brought north. A
combination of surface lows and troughs will bring exceptionally
moist air over the state beginning late Monday night. Heavy rain and
isolated thunderstorms are possible throughout this period. Models
have not converged on details yet, so exact locations, timing, and
rainfall amounts are not certain. Please be prepared for periods of
heavy rain this coming week.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through the
Internet (weather.gov/hawaii), local media, social media, or NOAA
Weather Radio broadcasts.

An updated outlook will be issued MOnday by 6 AM HST or sooner if
necessary.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 25 at 8:13PM EDT until October 26 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous
rip currents and large breaking waves expected in the surf
zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT
Thursday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT
Monday through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some
roads and low lying property including parking lots, parks,
lawns, and homes adjacent to the waterfront will experience
shallow flooding. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers
away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can
throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom causing
neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will continue to rise with a
King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-week. The
morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily tides.
King Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2 feet of
inundation above ground level in low- lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement,
dangerous rip currents and large breaking waves expected in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT
Thursday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 8 AM EDT
Monday through Monday evening.

mid week, especially around high tide in areas where dunes have
been compromised. NC-12 between the Basnight Bridge and Rodanthe

into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer or
surfer head first into the bottom causing neck and back
injuries.

King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-week. The
morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily tides.

property.

dangerous surf conditions.

* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal

flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts.

average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, one to two feet of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, Strong

creeks will observe minor coastal flooding. Some roads may

information regarding coastal flood impacts and closures.

currents, piers, jetties, and other hazardous areas. It may
sweep swimmers off their feet, making it difficult to return
to shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

lifeguards before entering the ocean for possible hazards you may
be swept into.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal New Hanover
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 25 at 7:46PM EDT until October 26 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one foot of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines
and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 4 to 7 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents expected along with a strong north
to south longshore current.

* WHERE...Coastal New Hanover County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM EDT Monday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Monday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM EDT Monday through Monday
evening.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok, and
Bethel.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 10 AM AKDT Monday.

coast, but gusts as high as 55 mph are expected to persist inland
up to Bethel. Strongest winds are expected late tonight, and winds
will begin to diminish through Monday morning. However, steady
southwesterly flow is expected to continue into midweek.

properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal

life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning and High Surf Advisory,
until 2 AM EDT Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through
late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 25 at 4:13AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
ESFHFO

A significant pattern change is expected Monday night through at
least Thursday as deep tropical moisture is brought north. A
combination of surface lows and troughs will bring exceptionally
moist air over the eastern end of the state beginning Monday night
and extending to all islands Tuesday. Heavy rain and thunderstorms
are possible throughout this period. Models have not converged on
details yet, so exact locations, timing, and rainfall amounts are not
certain. Please be prepared for periods of heavy rain this coming
week.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through the
Internet (weather.gov/hawaii), local media, social media, or NOAA
Weather Radio broadcasts.

An updated outlook will be issued Sunday by 6 PM HST or sooner if
necessary.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Palm Beach County
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 25 at 7:43AM EDT until October 27 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Moderate coastal flooding around periods of high tide,
reaching major flood stage on Monday and Tuesday. Dangerous surf
is expected, with breaker heights reaching 8 to 10 feet. Life
threatening rip currents are expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 AM Monday to 8 PM EDT
Tuesday. Coastal Flood Advisories will then be necessary
through much of next week after the peak of King Tides. For the
High Surf Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Wednesday. For the High Rip
Current Risk, through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
